claim: A production-grade Agent Skill for CI/CD enforces a fixed quality-gate pipeline (lint, type check, unit tests, build, integration tests, E2E, security audit, bundle size) through which no change may pass without completing every gate.
stance_target: SOPs can be encoded as rigid, mechanically-enforced Agent Skills rather than advisory prompts
scope_conditions: Node.js/TypeScript projects using GitHub Actions, as documented in the addyosmani/agent-skills open-source repo
quoted_support: No gate can be skipped. If lint fails, fix lint — don't disable the rule. If a test fails, fix the code — don't skip the test.

claim: The documented pattern for agentic CI integration is a closed feedback loop: CI failure output is copied verbatim and fed back to the coding agent, which fixes the issue and pushes again, re-triggering CI.
stance_target: continuous operation via event-driven triggers feeding agent loops
scope_conditions: general CI/CD with AI coding agents
quoted_support: The power of CI with AI agents is the feedback loop. When CI fails: Copy the failure output → Feed it to the agent... Agent fixes → pushes → CI runs again

claim: Feature flags are prescribed as the mechanism to decouple deployment from release in agent-driven CI/CD, with an explicit lifecycle requirement that every flag be assigned a cleanup date at creation to prevent flags becoming permanent technical debt.
stance_target: blast-radius control for autonomous agent deployments
quoted_support: Flag lifecycle: Create → Enable for testing → Canary → Full rollout → Remove the flag and dead code. Flags that live forever become technical debt — set a cleanup date when you create them.

claim: A staged rollout pipeline requires a defined 15-minute post-production monitoring window before a deployment is considered final, with automatic rollback triggered if errors are detected in that window.
stance_target: blast-radius containment mechanisms for autonomous deployment pipelines
quoted_support: Production deployment (manual trigger or auto after staging) → Monitor for errors (15-minute window) → Errors detected → Rollback / Clean → Done

claim: The skill assigns a named 'Build Cop' role responsible for fixing or reverting a broken build, explicitly not the person whose change caused the break, to prevent broken-build accumulation.
stance_target: organizational accountability patterns transferable to multi-agent software factories
quoted_support: When the build breaks, the Build Cop's job is to fix or revert — not the person whose change caused the break.

claim: CI should never have access to production secrets; separate secrets must be maintained for CI testing versus production deployment.
stance_target: security isolation in multi-agent build infrastructure
quoted_support: CI should never have production secrets. Use separate secrets for CI testing.

claim: A prescribed CI optimization order of impact is: cache dependencies, parallelize jobs, skip unrelated jobs via path filters, shard tests via matrix builds, then use larger runners -- applied in that priority sequence once a pipeline exceeds 10 minutes.
stance_target: cost and resource optimization for continuous agent operation
quoted_support: When the pipeline exceeds 10 minutes, apply these strategies in order of impact: Cache dependencies ... Run jobs in parallel ... Only run what changed ... Use matrix builds ... Optimize the test suite ... Use larger runners
